Thanks Neha / Marissa / Karthik —

Appreciate you taking a look at our proposed private VPC topology. We attached the current boundary diagram (PDF) and a short checklist of egress expectations. High-level asks:

- Confirm the control-plane/data-plane demarcation is compatible with Redwood's private deployment model (we have a requirement that control plane management traffic never traverses tenant data lanes).
- Confirm NAT/egress constraints for telemetry (we want metrics/logs to go to our observability tenant over a dedicated egress path).
- Any blockers for pinning model-serving VMs to the isolated data-plane subnets (we plan to use a dedicated subnets + node selectors).

We'd like sign-off (or list of actionable changes) by EOD Wednesday so our infra team can schedule the colo cutover next week.

Attachments: northstar_vpc_boundary_diagram_v1.pdf, controlplane-egress-checklist.xlsx

Alex —

Thanks for the diagram and checklist. Short summary of our review after a quick pass:

1) Control plane separation: diagram looks sound. Important note: Redwood's management/control-plane agents (agent-control-proxy) must be reachable over a management VLAN that is isolated from tenant data subnets and routed via the control-plane transit VPC. In practice that means the control-plane interface should terminate in the separate control subnet you marked as "mgmt-cp-1".

Action: please expose a /29 for planned control-plane hop (we call it cp-egress) and add a static route toward our management fabric.

2) KV cache and model-serving placement: pinning model-serving nodes to the isolated data-plane subnets is fine; just confirm that the nodes cannot source public egress directly. Redwood expects all external observability/metrics to traverse the approved egress path (see checklist). We'll keep KV cache peers inside the data plane; control-plane requests that touch dashboards will go over the mgmt path only.

3) Telemetry egress: the checklist covers destinations; one gap is TLS interception for our agent heartbeat. We require outbound 443 to telemetry.redwood-infra.com from the control-plane egress, with mTLS. Can you confirm your observability tenant can accept mTLS client certs?

4) ACL & DNS: suggest an explicit ACL for the control subnet that denies 0.0.0.0/0 egress except to the approved mgmt endpoints. Also we recommend a split-horizon DNS entry for internal model registry hostnames.

I've annotated the PDF with overlays and attached a short runbook fragment inline here. If you can iterate the diagram with the cp-egress /29 and add the mTLS endpoint for telemetry, I think we're close to sign-off.

Neha Kapoor

Quick operational checklist from my side:

- Canary policy: when you cutover, we'll route a small % of control-plane registration traffic over the management VLAN to sanity-check model manifests before opening full traffic. We need a 2-hour maintenance window to validate KV cache warm-up.
- SLA exception: NorthStar requested fixed public egress IPs for observability. That is doable but requires a /32 NAT allocation from your side or the colo provider; confirm who will supply that.
- Backup plan: if the mTLS handshake to telemetry fails, Redwood will temporarily fall back to a diagnostic-only collector that writes to an internal staging bucket (retention 7d) until the issue is resolved. Please ensure compliance with this behavior in your security docs.

I'll approve sign-off once Alex confirms the cp-egress /29 and NAT allocation plan.

Marissa Cole

Neha / Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed review and the annotated PDF. Quick replies to action items below: 

- cp-egress /29: we'll allocate 192.0.2.64/29 for cp-egress and add a static route toward your management fabric. I've attached an updated diagram (v2) to the Drive link (see related_links).
- mTLS telemetry: confirmed. Our observability tenant will accept mTLS client certs; infra team will provision certs and share the CA chain with Redwood ops.
- NAT / public egress IP: the colo will provide a single fixed IPv4 for egress (we'll provide the /32) — I'm logging this in JIRA INFRA-9123 for audit evidence and will circulate the screenshot when allocated.

One small ask: can Redwood add an explicit network ACL rule to deny data-plane initiated flows to control-plane mgmt endpoints except from the kube-proxy prefix? We prefer a deny-by-default on the control side with explicit allow for known management ranges.

If that works, please consider this thread signed off and we'll schedule cutover for Friday 06/25.
